subject: physics
question_text: Using the law of equipartition of energy, find the molar specific heat at constant volume (C_V) of a monoatomic gas.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Very Short Answer Question 14 (printed p.138). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: a monoatomic molecule has 3 degrees of freedom, so by equipartition U = (3/2)RT per mole; C_V = dU/dT = (3/2)R = 1.5 × 8.31 = 12.47 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, arithmetic verified.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Energy per mole
steps.margin_note: First mark. The step from ½k_BT per molecule to (3/2)RT per mole must be shown.
steps.why: By the law of equipartition each degree of freedom carries ½k_BT of energy per molecule, so ½RT per mole; a monoatomic molecule has 3 such degrees, giving a total internal energy of (3/2)RT for one mole.
common_mistakes: Using ½k_BT for a whole mole instead of scaling it to ½RT.
Taking 5 degrees of freedom, which belongs to a diatomic molecule, not a monoatomic one.

recall.must_convey: That a monoatomic molecule has 3 degrees of freedom, so by equipartition the internal energy of one mole is (3/2)RT.
accept: 3 degrees of freedom for a monoatomic molecule
U equals three by two R T
each degree of freedom carries half k T
reject: C_V equals three by two R

steps.memory_tip: 3 degrees, each half k_BT: 3 × ½ = 3/2, so U = (3/2)RT per mole.

steps.label: C_V value
steps.margin_note: Second mark. C_V = (3/2)R is the answer; adding the numeric value, 12.47 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, shows you can evaluate it.
steps.why: C_V is defined as the rate of change of internal energy with temperature at constant volume; since U = (3/2)RT is proportional to T, its derivative is the constant (3/2)R, which equals 1.5 × 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
common_mistakes: Reporting C_V as (5/2)R, which is the diatomic value.

recall.must_convey: That C_V for a monoatomic gas is (3/2)R, which is about 12.47 joule per mole per kelvin.
accept: C_V equals three by two R
differentiate U with respect to T
reject: U equals three by two R T

steps.memory_tip: C_V is the slope of U against T: since U = (3/2)RT, the slope is just (3/2)R.

insider_note: State both the general result C_V = (3/2)R and its number, 12.47 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ — the number alone with no derivation loses the first mark.
